title: This Shark Swims 2 km/h Forever or It Drowns 🦈
description:
Why do some sharks drown if they stop swimming? Great white, mako and whale sharks use ram ventilation, swimming with their mouths open so water flows over their gills, while nurse sharks can rest on the sea floor and pump water with their cheeks.

topic: Why do some sharks drown if they stop swimming?
script: This shark drowns if you make it stop swimming. Wait, a fish that drowns? Sharks pull oxygen out of water as it flows over their gills. A nurse shark can lie still on the sea floor and pump water in with its cheeks. But a great white can't do that. Neither can makos or whale sharks. They use ram ventilation. They swim with their mouths slightly open so water gets pushed over their gills. Stop swimming, and the water stops. No water, no oxygen. So even while it's resting, a great white keeps cruising at about two kilometers an hour. That's slower than you walk! Most sharks can take a break, though. So which shark would you rather be? The one that naps on the sand, or the one that can never stop?
key_facts: Great white, mako and whale sharks are obligate ram ventilators: they must swim so water flows over their gills (Britannica, Live Science)
Nurse sharks can rest on the bottom and pump water over their gills with their cheek muscles (Britannica)
Most kinds of sharks won't die if they stop swimming (Britannica)
Tracked white sharks at Mossel Bay averaged about 0.5 m/s over ground, swimming speed estimated ~1.2x that, roughly 2 km/h (Johnson et al. 2009)
